c.v: ESP32-S3's low-power management involves the following components:
Power management unit: controls the power supply to three power domain categories
For a complete list of 10 power domains grouped in these three power domain categories, see
Power isolation unit: isolates different power domains, so powered up and powered down domains do not affect each other.
Low-power clocks: provide clocks to power domains working in low-power modes.
RTC timer: logs the status of the RTC main state machine in dedicated registers.
timer: wakes up the ULP co-processors at a predefined time.
timer: wakes up the touch sensor at a predefined time.
On-Chip Sensors and Analog Signal Processing
"always-on" retention registers: These registers are always powered up and are not affected by any low-power modes, thus can be used for storing data that cannot be lost.
22 x "always-on" pins: These pins are always powered up and not affected by any low-power modes.
They can be used as wakeup sources when the chip is working in the low-power modes (for details, please refer to
), or can be used as regular GPIOs (for details, please refer to
IO MUX and GPIO Matrix (GPIO, IO MUX)
SRAM that works under RTC fast clock (rtc_fast_clk), which can be used as extended memory or to store ULP co-processor directives and data.
SRAM that works under CPU clock (CPU_CLK), which can be used as extended memory.
Voltage regulators: regulate the power supply to different power domains.
